title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Clients Under a Disability
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is negotiating a complex settlement for a client with a known cognitive disability. The paralegal feels the client does not fully understand the consequences of the settlement despite multiple simple explanations. What should the paralegal do?
options: Sign the settlement on the client's behalf because the paralegal knows it is a good deal.
Maintain the relationship as best as possible, but consider whether a litigation guardian needs to be appointed to protect the client's interests.
Withdraw immediately because the client lacks the legal capacity to give instructions.
Ask the opposing counsel to explain the settlement to the client.
questions.explain: Rule 3.02 dictates that a paralegal shall maintain a normal professional relationship with a client under a disability as far as reasonably possible. If the client cannot comprehend instructions affecting their legal rights, the paralegal may need to take steps to have a lawfully authorized representative (e.g., a litigation guardian) appointed.
